answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Bond with a decaying refund schedule flips the bet — a refund that shrinks the sooner you misbehave — and the ripple lands on the attacker instead. What makes this stick is that a refund that shrinks the sooner you misbehave cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the dawn of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the signal of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
